title: join-rules host pid lock is never stolen and never liveness-checked, so any unclean stop (kill, taskkill, crash, power loss, reboot) leaves raw/webinars/join-rules-host.pid and every later start is refused until a human deletes it
area: scripts/webinar/join-rules-host.ts acquireHostLock; scripts/webinar/join-rules-api-host.ts (handlers cover exit, SIGINT, SIGTERM only)
evidence:
Probe on 4a64ae7: writeFileSync(<dir>/join-rules-host.pid, "999999
") then acquireHostLock(<dir>) throws: "join-rules host: <dir>join-rules-host.pid exists, so another host owns this state directory (or it crashed). Not starting. If no host is running, delete that file and retry." The pid is written but never read. On Windows SIGTERM/taskkill /F/service stop do not run handlers, so the file survives; raw/webinars is on disk so it survives reboot too. Message is clear and names the file, but recovery needs a human after every unclean stop (R1: recover after interruption).
fix_direction: On EEXIST read the recorded pid; if process.kill(pid,0) throws ESRCH treat the lock as stale and replace it (still via exclusive create after unlink, to stay race-safe); keep refusing when the pid is alive or the file is unparseable. Test: stale pid 999999 is replaced, live pid (process.pid) is refused.
